2107822293653041659.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a voiceover or song with a spoken line (the audio file) and its transcript, 10-12 small objects that sum up my life, two silhouettes to light like a heat camera (a head in profile and a raised hand), and the 3 words I want to land hardest. If I skip any, use the defaults: vinyl, book, camera, cat, coin, game controller, cap, heart, money, plant, clapperboard, skateboard; free CC0 silhouettes from Openverse; action, intention, curiosity.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 20 second 4:3 film, 1440x1080 at 60fps, cut to the voice. Off-white paper, black, one red, one yellow, Geist for every word. Film grain on everything, a soft vignette, and a camera that never rests: a slow handheld float under everything plus a slow push inside every scene.
No scene cuts to the next: each handoff starts on the exact last frame of the scene before. The only hard cuts are the beat flips on the last word.
Every object is pixel art you draw yourself: a 16x16 grid per object, every cell a hand-placed colour, rendered as a 3D block (a darker extrusion down-right, a thin bevel on every cell) with a soft contact shadow.
The silhouettes are lit like a heat camera: the heat comes from how thick the body is at each point, so the nose, the hair and the fingertips run cooler, plus one hotspot and a slow moving noise, mapped through a black > red > orange > cream ramp. The edge stays razor sharp, with a soft glow outside it.
Motion rules: nothing pops in (eased glides of about 0.5s with a soft start), fast moves get real motion blur instead of ghost copies, and captions type with the voice behind a block cursor.
Banned: stock footage, AI video, 3D camera moves, particles, glitch.
</direction>

<structure>
Hang every scene on the transcript's word timings (measure them with faster-whisper word timestamps, one short chunk at a time):
1. The first word fills a yellow card. The card wipes off to the left and the question types underneath on two centred lines that glide to stay centred as they grow, the key word underlined in red as it's spoken.
2. The objects streak past in lanes above and below the words, a cyan four-point flare sweeps in, then the page burns away: black closes in from the edges onto the head, behind a hot red edge.
3. The head heats up on black while the answer types low on the left. A thin white orbit draws itself around the head, its far half passing behind it. On the last word, paper blooms out from inside the head with the objects in it, and the camera falls through: the head rushes past the lens until the paper is all we see.
4. The objects sit on a tilted ring seen in perspective (the front ones bigger and lower, drawn last), slowly turning, each one bobbing; the coin flips and lands with sparks.
5. On each of the 3 words, that object flies out of the ring to the left and grows, the page floods black from it, and the word types beside it (camera: a red shutter star; book: a red ribbon sweep; record: two white orbits and red notes). Then the flood drains back into the object as it flies home, and the camera dives closer into the ring. Put each hero object in the slot that is front-left when its word lands.
6. The ring pulls in a touch, bursts outward, every object turns to ink, and ink blots grow and swallow the page.
7. The hand rises into frame, hot, with the line split either side of it. The heart drops into its palm, then lifts to the centre at the size the next scene holds it.
8. The last word, one letter per beat, the background flipping paper / black / red, the heart holding its place across the cut, the centre object morphing pixel by pixel into the next one.
9. Thin brush strokes sweep through, the letters drift apart and float, then settle back into the word with the heart above it. The camera keeps pushing through the hold.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. Bake each pixel sprite once to an offscreen canvas (the extrusion layers, then the face), then draw it scaled and rotated.
3. The heat: precompute each silhouette's base heat once (a distance transform of the mask, held at the edge value outside it so nothing dark bleeds in when it is upscaled). Every frame, add the hotspot and two octaves of value noise at quarter resolution, map it through a 256-step lookup, upscale it, and cut it with the full-resolution mask.
4. The fall through the head: draw the ring scene into an offscreen layer, mask it with the head scaled up about a point inside the skull, and grow that scale on a cubed curve until the head covers the frame. The ring inside zooms less than the head does, so it reads as depth.
5. The pixel morph: pair every cell of object A with a cell of object B and glide each one's position and colour, with a small random delay per cell.
6. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes, then lay the original audio back on with ffmpeg.
</build>

<gotchas>
A mask PNG with no alpha channel fills the whole box with heat, so put the silhouette in the alpha. A limb cut by the photo's border shows as a straight edge, so extend the mask past the frame. A handoff only reads as smooth when the last frame of one scene is the first frame of the next: draw the outgoing scene under the transition, and give scenes that show the same ring one shared zoom function. A flood that's still retreating when the next scene starts reads as a hard cut, so let it finish first. A fast ease-out flood reads as a jump; use a soft start.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, measure the word timings, then show me 8 stills before you render.
</start>

2118149077842133334.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for my animal or topic ("Why is the X the most disturbing animal in the ocean?", "Why is X terrifying?"), or pitch 3, each with 5 true facts that get worse as they go. Ask which image model I have (GPT Image 2 or any model that takes a reference image at 4K, about $0.03 an image) and which voice I have (ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free). Then write the script and the shot list with seconds, and show me both before anything costs money.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1080x1920, 60 fps, 30-35 s vertical Short in the style of the big narrated animal-facts channels where a guy in a hoodie with a mic pops into every scene. Here everything is a flat 2D cartoon: thick dark brown outlines (#1f1418), flat colours, simple cel shading, big round googly eyes.
The host: a cartoon young man with messy brown hair, glasses, a plain heather grey hoodie with no logo, dark jeans, white sneakers, always holding a black mic.
- He is about 1000-1050 px tall on screen. His feet sit below the frame edge, so he is cut off at the shins.
- He pops up from below the frame in 0.32 s with an overshoot ease.
- His mouth flaps on the voice whenever he talks to camera.
- His face always stays above the caption pill.
The animal: one character in 9 poses (neutral, shocked, angry, plus costume poses for the facts: old with a beard and cane, a powdered wig, a teen with braces, drunk, a front view of the face, defeated on a plate). One costume per fact is the joke.
A new place every 1.5-3 s. Never repeat a composition.
Something always moves:
- Animals swim with a tail wave and bob ±10 px.
- The camera pushes in 2-4% per shot.
- Pose swaps squash.
- Hits shake the frame.
Titles are one or two big words per beat in Luckiest Guy (Google Fonts), 104-190 px at y 430, tilted ±0.03-0.05 rad:
- They wobble ±0.025 rad.
- The outline is 0.22 of the size in #1f1418, with a darker copy of the colour 0.09 of the size underneath.
- Colours are pairs of fill and shadow: yellow #ffd21f/#c27a10, red #ff4a3d/#8e1a14, white #ffffff/#9aa6b4, pink #ff7ab8/#a8336d, green #7dff6a/#2e9a2a.
Captions:
- 1-4 words in a white pill at y 1470: Luckiest Guy 66 px, dark text, a 7 px outline, pill height 1.55x the text.
- The key word is yellow with a dark outline.
- The pill pops from 0.82 to 1 in 0.13 s.
A red marker ellipse circles the animal when its name is said.
Banned: photoreal cutouts mixed into cartoon art, a real person's face, the real channel's logo or name on screen, a still frame over 1 s, the host covering the animal's face on its key word.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: 30-35 s, about 115 words at about 3.5 words a second. Times are from a 33.5 s film; scale them to the voice.
0-1.9 s, the hook "Why is the X the most disturbing animal in the ocean?":
- The animal glides in from off screen in 0.75 s while the host pops up bottom right, already talking.
- On the animal's name: a red ring, the name as a title, and the host swaps to pointing at it for 0.7 s.
1.9-3.7 s: a punch-in on "disturbing". The water is graded red, the angry pose, an impact starburst, the word in red.
3.7-8.2 s, fact 1, the shocking number:
- A counter rolls up to it.
- Then a comparison everyone gets ("older than America") shown as a costume pose and a prop that springs in.
8.2-12.7 s, facts 2 and 3 played as gags:
- One is a costume in a new place.
- One is a race the animal loses. On "slower than you walk", the host strolls past it.
12.7-15.6 s: the gross detail, with a zoom into the face.
15.6-16.7 s: "But it gets worse." A red alarm grade with a pulsing vignette. The animal yells into the lens and the host swaps from talking to horrified.
16.7-21 s, the worst fact:
- The host cowers behind the victim, which then vanishes in a poof.
- An x-ray shot shows what is inside.
21-27.7 s: the human angle, each line with a person from the cast acting it out. The host joins in (drunk next to the drunk Viking).
27.7-29 s: someone happily eats it while the host turns green and gags.
29-33.5 s: the callback joke that ties back to the hook. The host talks to camera, then cracks up on the last word. Hold 1.15 s after the last word.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy, soundfile. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Art, 4 images in total (about $0.12). Every prompt starts with "Match the exact art style of the reference image: flat 2D cartoon, thick dark brown outlines, flat colours with simple cel shading, big expressive googly eyes, clean vector look". Feed the first sheet you like back in as the style reference for the rest.
- Animal sheet: 1:1 at 4K, "a 3 by 3 pose sheet of the SAME cartoon X, 9 separate poses on plain pure white, plenty of white space, nothing touching, no grid lines, no text, no ground shadows", every pose a full side view facing right except the front face.
- Cast sheet: 1:1 at 4K, 9 different characters and props for the facts, same wording.
- Background grid: 9:16 at 4K, "a 3 by 3 grid of 9 equal tall vertical panels separated by thin white gutters, each panel an EMPTY scene, no characters, no text, keep the lower middle open".
- Host sheet: 9:16 at 4K, 9 full-body poses at the same size: (1) facing the viewer, mic below the chin, mouth CLOSED, (2) EXACTLY the same pose with only the mouth WIDE OPEN, (3) talking and pointing to the side, (4) horrified with a hand on the cheek, (5) crouching and cowering with sweat drops, (6) running in side view facing right, (7) laughing and leaning back, (8) gagging with a green face holding a toothpick of food, (9) drunk with spiral eyes.
3. Cutouts:
- Flood the white from the border (seeds every 64 px around the edge) with a floating range of 7, so soft glows go too.
- Feather a 3 px band outside the shapes with alpha = clamp((250 - min(R,G,B)) / 150). Un-mix the white from that band: colour = (c - 255(1 - a)) / a.
- Group the pieces by the grid cell their centre falls in and drop pieces under 150 px.
- Split the background grid on its white gutters (rows and columns whose minimum channel averages over 232). Crop 4 px in, cover-fit to 1080x1920 with Lanczos, unsharp mask (radius 2, 60%).
4. Host lip-sync:
- Align pose 2 onto pose 1 by template-matching the glasses and eyes. Paste only its mouth onto pose 1 through a feathered ellipse (sigma 4). Now open and closed are the same drawing, so the outline never wobbles.
- Mouth track at 60 fps from the voice: RMS per frame, smoothed over 3 frames. Open when it is over (70th percentile in dB - 15) and over 0.55x the loudest frame within ±0.1 s.
- Hold every state at least 3 frames. Break open runs longer than 14 frames with a 3-frame close every 12 frames. That gives about 8 flips a second.
- Anchor every host pose by its feet and its head centre x (the alpha centre of the top 28% of the cutout), so pose swaps never jump. Measure that per pose.
5. Voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4 with the timestamps endpoint, a calm deep documentary narrator, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, one take (about 300 credits for 600 characters).
- Cut pauses (10 ms frames under -40 dB, longer than 0.2 s) down to their first and last 0.06 s, with 8 ms fades.
- Then atempo 1.15 and a 0.15 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the character alignment through the same cuts and tempo. When a start lands after the next word's start, pull it back.
- Free route: Kokoro, then whisper for the word times.
6. Film: one HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV with the sound times. One function per shot.
- Sprite tail wave: draw the cutout in 28 vertical slices. Each slice moves dy = sin(8t - 4.5u) * wig * k, where k = (max(0, u - 0.3) / 0.7)^1.5 and wig is 3-14 px.
- Pop: 1 - 0.6 e^(-9Δt) cos(20Δt). Pose-swap kick: 1 + a e^(-10Δt) cos(22Δt), with a = 0.1-0.22. Shake: A e^(-7Δt) sin(61Δt), with A = 22-34 px.
- Props drawn in code: a rolling number counter, a waving flag, a flipping calendar, green fumes, buzzing flies, confetti, red rings, arrows, an impact starburst, poof clouds, bubbles.
- Red alarm grade: grayscale(.5) sepia(1) hue-rotate(-35deg) saturate(3.2) brightness(.55).
- X-ray: grayscale(1) invert(1) sepia(1) hue-rotate(150deg) saturate(3.5) on #071a2e with a 60 px cyan grid and a scan line.
- Look up repeated words by their occurrence (the third "and"), or cuts land on the wrong line.
7. Check, render, sound:
- Contact sheets of 12-15 frames at key words before rendering. Fix covered faces, the host over the animal's face, and titles off screen.
- Render 60 fps with 8 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, then libx264 CRF 19.
- Music: a quirky piano mystery bed, free on Pixabay, with the voice 11-14 dB over it in every phrase.
- Mixkit SFX, one per event, placed by their peaks: a pop on every title, a whoosh when the host or the animal enters, a hit on the big beats, a bite, a boing, a sad trombone on the fails, a poof, bubbles.
- Mix to -14 LUFS.
</build>

<gotchas>
- A plain hue tint for the red alarm turned blue water green. Sepia first, then hue-rotate.
- Long titles overflow at 160 px. Split them into two beats ("OLDER THAN", then "AMERICA" in red).
- The host walking past on the key word hid the animal's face. Time his pass after the key word, keep him lower and smaller (0.62 scale), or draw him behind.
- Photoreal sticker animals with code eyes read as slop next to a real presenter. One flat cartoon style for everything fixes it.
- If the two talking poses differ by more than the mouth, swapping whole images makes the outline wobble. Paste the mouth only.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my animal or topic, or pitch 3, then show me the script and the shot list.
</start>

2105957241148813340.prompt:
Build an interactive 3D jelly pufferfish (fugu) as a single self-contained HTML page using three.js from a CDN.

The fish is a soft-body gummy sitting on a table. Model the body as one closed icosphere-topology skin with two rest shapes per vertex: a calm fish (blunt round head, body tapering to a short tail stalk, slightly flattened belly) and a fully inflated ball (sphere with the same tail stalk sticking out). Blend between them with an "inflation" value. Simulate with XPBD at a fixed 1/600 s substep (frame-rate independent): edge-length constraints, a global volume constraint, a soft global shape-matching pull toward the blended rest shape (rotation via polar decomposition, gently leaning upright), ground collision with friction, and damping applied to the wobble (velocity relative to the body's mean) so it jiggles but settles in about a second. Render with one Loop-subdivision pass for a smooth surface.

Behaviour: tapping the fish startles it. It gulps air three times (mouth opens on each gulp, small overshoot) until it is a round ball, stays puffed about 4 seconds, then slowly deflates while blowing iridescent bubbles from its mouth. Dragging grabs and stretches the jelly locally; dragging empty space orbits the camera; wheel or pinch zooms.

Details: ~260 soft spines that lie flat and hidden when calm, pop up one by one (staggered) as it inflates, wobble on their own springs, bend against the table, and lift the ball so it stands on its spines. Big glossy eyes (gold-green iris, large pupil, white catchlight) that follow the cursor. Puckered lips with a tiny white beak. Translucent ray-striped fins: fluttering pectorals, swaying tail fan, rippling dorsal and anal fins, all faster when alarmed. Dark freckles on the back, pale belly, a few air bubbles trapped inside the jelly.

Look: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, clearcoat and sheen for a candy-gummy look; a soft environment map; a soft colored shadow with a faint caustic on a floor that matches the page background. Flavour presets Yuzu, Ramune, Momo, Matcha. Editorial "Material Studies" layout: big italic serif title "Fugu Jelly.", a side panel with flavour swatches, Firmness and Wobble sliders, Startle / Calm / Reset buttons, ¼ speed and Sound toggles, and live readouts for volume, spine angle and mood. Synthesized WebAudio sounds for gulps, a boing on tap, a hiss while deflating and tiny bubble pops. Responsive down to phone width.

2109515393220083912.prompt:
架空の大型ロケット（2段式の液体ロケット＋固体ブースター2本、白い機体、名前なし）と
その射点について、CAD図面と Blender 動画を作ってください。

【図面】2D の DXF のみ（3Dモデルの書き出しは不要）。単位 mm、A2 の図枠と表題欄つき。
線は青緑系の「電子の図面」風にし、プレビュー画像は濃紺の背景にする。
1. 射点配置図 S=1:500（ロケットを原点に置き、実際の位置で描く。
移動発射台・排煙溝・アンビリカルタワー・避雷塔・照明塔・水タンク・建屋・海岸線）
2. 射点立面図（南から）S=1:400
3. ロケット外形図・断面図 S=1:250
特記事項に「架空の機体・射場のイメージで、実在の図面ではない」と書く。
寸法は Python の形状モジュール1つで決め、図面と動画の両方がそれを読み込む。

【動画】Blender（EEVEE）、1920×1080・24fps・本編20秒＋ロゴ3.5秒、音つき MP4。
1. 暗闇の床に、シアンに光る射点配置図が中心から走査されて描かれる（真上から）
2. 図面の線が光のワイヤーとして立ち上がる
3. 光の粒（Geometry Nodes）が渦を巻いて昇り、発射台・タワー・ロケットが下から積み上がる
（積み上がった高さより下だけが実体になる。カメラは寄る）
4. 図面がマス目ごとにデジタルに溶け、夜の射点が現れる（海・丘・星空。カメラは引く）。
照明塔が点いて白い機体が浮かび、塔の頂部の赤い灯が明滅する
5. アクセスアームが離れる → カウントダウン → 点火 → リフトオフ。
炎は発光する円錐、噴煙は排煙溝と発射台から湧き、上昇する機体の後ろに煙の柱が残る
6. 上昇するロケットを海の上から見上げたところでタイトル → 最後に指定のロゴ
音は外部素材を使わず Python で合成する
（電子音の BGM、波、カウントダウンの電子音、点火から上昇までの轟音、タイトルの和音）。

【進め方】
- 図面のプレビュー画像を目で見て、文字の重なりを直す
- 本番の前にテスト静止画を数枚描いて確認する（照明の明るさ、炎や光の白飛び）
- 本番レンダーは軽い設定で、PC を休ませながら回す。始める前に所要時間を伝えて了承を取る

2114745463736082828.prompt:
Create a spectacular 4:3 Jujutsu Kaisen AMV centered on Satoru Gojo, using the supplied images and music. Match the final video's duration exactly to the full soundtrack.

EDITING & ANIMATION:
Analyze the music's rhythm, structure, energy and emotional progression. Animate the supplied images into dynamic cinematic sequences with expressive character motion, dramatic camera movements, parallax and seamless transitions. Creatively select, crop, reframe, combine and revisit images throughout the edit. Build an intense anime opening with powerful visual storytelling, synchronized precisely to the music.

DYNAMIC GRID:
Use a constantly evolving manga-inspired grid with variable cell sizes, shapes and arrangements. Mix large hero panels, small square cells, narrow strips, irregular rectangles and occasional diagonal divisions. Freely expand, shrink, split, merge and rearrange cells according to the music. Alternate between dense multi-cell compositions, striking asymmetrical layouts and occasional full-frame hero moments. Allow different images, perspectives and moments to coexist across cells. Keep panel boundaries crisp and compositions visually coherent.

VISUAL EFFECTS:
Create intense, layered effects inspired by Gojo Satoru's powers and the visual identity of Jujutsu Kaisen. Explore spatial distortion, Infinity, Six Eyes, cursed energy, Blue, Red and Hollow Purple through inventive motion graphics, impact frames, dimensional fractures and cinematic transitions. Blend style infections spreading across neighboring cells with temporal echoes, frame repetitions, speed ramps, freezes and rhythmic chain reactions. Let effects interact creatively with the grid and occasionally break beyond panel boundaries.

CREATIVE DIRECTION:
Make this feel like a premium, visually groundbreaking Jujutsu Kaisen anime opening. Capture Gojo's overwhelming power, confidence, elegance and mysterious presence. Let the supplied images and soundtrack guide every creative decision, including pacing, visual treatments, transitions, color grading and effect intensity. Avoid repetitive editing patterns or generic templates. Balance explosive action with striking moments of visual clarity. Preserve Gojo's recognizable identity, facial features, costume and the artistic style of the supplied images.

AUDIO:
Use the supplied music as the primary soundtrack, uninterrupted from beginning to end. Synchronize animation, grid transformations, camera movements and visual effects to its beats, melodies, transitions and emotional peaks.
No typography, text, letters, numbers or watermarks.

2119392067646345249.prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: an interactive, fully procedural 3D robotic giant squid called "Architeuthis AX-10" (brand mark "Teuthis"), rendered with three.js r170 loaded via an importmap from jsDelivr. No external models, textures or images; every part is generated in code at load time. Target quality: a premium product-simulator / engineering teardown page with thousands of real moving parts.

LOOK
- Bright studio look: near-white background (canvas-drawn, soft lavender corner gradients, faint dot grid top-right), white glossy shells with clearcoat, near-black mechanical internals, violet accents (#8a4dff) and glowing violet emissives.
- No tone mapping; calibrate lights so white shells stay just below 1.0 and keep visible shading (no blown-out whites). Hemisphere + key directional light with soft PCF shadows (2048 map) + fill + rim + RoomEnvironment PMREM reflections. Invisible shadow-catcher floor plus a soft contact shadow blob.
- Post: EffectComposer with HalfFloat MSAA target, GTAO (hide background, floor, emissives and decorative lines during the AO prepass), UnrealBloom with a high threshold (~1.5) so only emissive parts glow, OutputPass.
- Procedural surface-detail shader injected into MeshPhysicalMaterial via onBeforeCompile: clustered drill holes, short slots, rivet rows parallel to every panel edge, and a dark seam groove along panel borders. Geometry builders write per-vertex metric surface coordinates and distance-to-panel-edge attributes so holes stay round and evenly sized; antialias with fwidth; holes kill clearcoat; per-instance seed so instanced links differ.

GEOMETRY TOOLKIT
- revPanel(): surface-of-revolution panel with real thickness (outer, inner, flat-shaded rims), profile from Catmull-Rom-smoothed points, angular range, offset. Plus extruded gears, spline tubes/cables, rounded boxes. Merge each part's geometry per material.

MODEL (body frame: +z toward the arms, +y dorsal)
- Mantle (~1.2 m ogive cone) on a neck joint so it can swing relative to the head: 28 separate shell panels with gaps, hinge knuckles, violet tiles, LEDs and vent slots; a hinged glass window along the top that opens 110° (hinge axis computed from the panel edge); under it 8 lit violet piston bays, each with 16–24 black components, pistons with steel rods, capacitors, coils, headers; dark inner hull; tail cap with glowing tip; collar ring with 60 bolts.
- Head (slightly enlarged sub-frame): 15 shell strips, each auto-populated without overlaps with printed glyphs (Y, arrows, T, X), inset hatches with four screws, vent grilles, sensor ports with LEDs, steel grab rails, seam hinges; two antennas at the back.
- Visor plate on 6 steel lift pins. Under it a deep head cavity lined with a glowing violet motherboard: finned heat-sink processor, 7-blade spinning cooling fan, 3-ring gimballed gyro (rings spin on different axes), capacitor bank, twin steel coolant lines, cable harnesses to the eyes, ribbon cable, 3-gear head drive with correct ratios, and a sensor deck with a sonar puck on standoffs that lifts away.
- Two eyes: white donut housings with bolts, black glossy lens, glowing violet rings and glyph, 4 threaded telescoping barrel rings, 10-blade iris (each blade pivots), sapphire glass dome with rim.
- Dark hub under the head with ring gear, motors and cables; a central siphon with 3 nested telescoping sleeves and a 10-blade turbine whose glow follows thrust.

ARMS
- 8 arms (20 links) + 2 longer tentacles (30 links, clubbed). Links are built in unit-radius space with length = 2 × radius so everything scales uniformly; radius tapers from ~6 cm.
- Per link, GPU-instanced pieces: white or violet shell (two variants), ball joint with steel pin, chain side plates, two violet roller wheels with dark hubs on the oral side, plus occasional side modules, dorsal tiles and violet bands. Update all instance matrices on the CPU every frame.
- Quaternion forward kinematics: root frame spreads around a crown axis blended between the body axis and world-down (so arms splay octopus-like on the floor); per-link curvature = base bend + log-spiral tip term (curvature ∝ 1/remaining length, rollers inside the curl) + travelling wave; per-arm random variation. Blend poses: standing, jetting bundle, single arm stretched. Auto-ground the body so the lowest link touches the floor.

RIG AND TIMELINE
- Every rigid part is a registered group with base transform, chapter offsets and an explode vector; explode cascades with per-part delays, ease5 and free spin. Spin phases use the integral of a trapezoid speed profile so everything is deterministic.
- A pure stateAt(t) function (no accumulation) drives a ~28 s loop: jetting in mantle-first, settle and stand, Optics (barrels extend, iris cycles, dome lifts), Head core (visor lifts, then deck lifts while the camera slowly orbits the open cavity), Arm (one arm straightens, shells lift off the roller chain, spiral tip), Mantle (glass window opens over lit bays), Siphon (sleeves telescope, turbine spins up), Teardown (all parts free with a 360° turntable), Reassembly, Launch (arms bundle, jet off).
- Per-chapter camera shots computed in body axes with eased blends; decorative thin orbit lines with node markers around the camera target.

UI (HTML/CSS/SVG overlay, Inter Tight + IBM Plex Mono)
- Logo top-left, "Live sim" pill top-right, centered model line + title "Colossal Squid, Lens to Siphon" + date, chapter pills, left nav with sub-lines, right telemetry cards (mantle pressure kPa with 6 s sparkline computed from stateAt, jet thrust bar, arm load bars for 10 arms from real curvature, battery), bottom status "Chapter · NN% apart" with progress track and timecode.
- 3D-anchored callouts: anchor dot on the real part, leader line, white label card; two columns with collision spacing.
- Clicking a pill/nav item seeks the timeline with a smooth camera blend; drag to orbit (free camera); double-click or R returns to auto camera; space pauses; click the track to seek. Responsive phone layout, prefers-reduced-motion support, adaptive quality governor (fewer GTAO samples, then DPR 1, then GTAO off).

CAPTURE AND AUDIO
- Expose https://window.sim.seek/(t) for deterministic frame capture (capture mode: no rAF loop, CSS transitions off). Render 1920×1080 at 60 fps with headless Playwright, sampling the timeline at 1.68× so the video is exactly 17 s; encode H.264 CRF 17 with AAC audio.
- Original synthesized score (numpy/scipy, no samples), one bar = one chapter so every change lands on a downbeat, plus synced sound design: jet roar, servos, lens clicks, visor hiss, fan spin-up, gear ticks, gyro tinks, chain clatter, glass ting, piston thumps, turbine spin-up, teardown impact with hundreds of part clinks, reverse swell into reassembly, launch roar. Normalize to about −21 LUFS.

2113344709682663503.prompt:
Apply a dark neon glitch-art effect to the attached video (Python + ffmpeg, frame by frame):

1. Cut out the subject with rembg (isnet-anime for anime/illustration, isnet-general-use for real footage). Make the background pure black.
2. Posterize the subject to 5 brightness levels and recolor it with a 3-color palette on black:
main color for cool/neutral areas (cyan #14b8f0), mid color (violet #6438c4), accent for warm/red areas (magenta #ff2ad4).
Keep it dark: most of the image black or navy, only the highlights glow. Let the color-patch edges crawl slightly with noise.
3. Add a magenta rim light on the subject's left edge.
4. Datamosh: wherever the current frame is empty, keep the previous frame shifted a few px down and faded (melting ghost trails). Also copy ~3% of 24px blocks from the previous frame with a small random offset.
5. Vertical drips: in ~30% of the columns, smear bright pixels upward (up to ~300px) and downward (~150px). Mix 2–8px wide drips with thin vertical scratch lines in the palette colors, denser near the subject.
6. Light grain + vignette. Keep the original resolution and fps, export as H.264 MP4.

Generate an original vaporwave-glitch soundtrack (~-12 LUFS) / make it a seamless loop where the last 1s drips into the first 1s column by column.

2113716424887661034.prompt:
Build a cinematic 3D animation of a white Tesla Roadster performing a rocket-assisted stunt inside a massive nighttime test facility.

Start with a wide shot revealing a towering curved ramp supported by exposed steel scaffolding. Add red illuminated track edges, road markings, and industrial floodlights.

Follow the Roadster as it accelerates up the ramp, climbs vertically, and launches into open air.

At the highest point, switch to a dramatic low-angle close-up. Fire the downward-facing thrusters. Show bright exhaust and thick, rolling smoke that expands naturally beneath the car.

Bring it down onto the track, let the suspension compress on landing, then pull the camera back as it drives forward through the clearing smoke.

Keep the white bodywork readable throughout. Control headlight bloom. Make the wheels rotate correctly and keep the vehicle’s shape consistent between shots.

Add subtle circular HUD gauges for altitude and G-force.

16 seconds. Vertical 9:16 framing. Smooth camera movement.

Make it look expensive. The launch and thruster
